question: Whether v5 majority coverage permits omission when senses 1–9 share separation/departure and sense 10 has directly documented older copy/reproduce → humorous imitation history.
reason: The precise v5 historical-residual provision covers a modern lexical meaning explained by historical semantic development even when the current expression is not archaic. Etymonline documents the relevant copying-to-imitation development. This permits an explicit exclusion of sense 10 rather than invented feature extraction or a false homograph claim. The other nine meanings can be presented through removal/departure, with sudden growth through the familiar flight metaphor. The earlier clean report accepted omission too readily under that explicit majority/classification rule.
constraints: Preserve the authentic original A response unchanged. This adjudication does not retroactively edit that response or pretend the core was reviewed there.
Include all nine applicable exact sense-title branches, and classify sense 10 once as a historical-residual exclusion in the core introduction under the current v5 layout.
Do not label contemporary British imitation as obsolete or claim a separate etymological homograph.
For growth, use the flight metaphor; do not imply that a business physically separates or must have previously stagnated.
The added current core requires genuine affected-area independent review, including any dependency changes; no presumed pass.

source_basis.basis: Majority requirement and historical-residual clause, including historical semantic change rather than only current archaism.
Directly read original history records older copying/reproduction followed by imitation/caricature.
